clue.text: Rook near observation post snapped by twitching circle

indicators.note: something snapped up by another is taken inside it, so the twitch wraps the rook and post

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitching
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
OP is the military abbreviation for observation post

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a rook near a lookout and photographs it amid a twitchy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitching' and 'Rook' suggest birdwatching ('twitchers'), but twitching is just TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude, each a circle round the globe.

clue.text: Middle-eastern high-fliers, during craze, regularly worship actor

indicators.note: the airline sits during, that is within, the word for a craze

parts.note: a bug is a craze or enthusiasm, as in 'the travel bug'
El Al is Israel's national airline, flyers from the Middle East

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of worship, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Fans worship a star as pilots from the Middle East catch a craze.
explanation.walkthrough: Bela Lugosi was the Hungarian-born actor famous as Dracula.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Lugosi was a screen performer, best known for playing Count Dracula in 1931.

clue.text: Exercises keep Nick, doing somersault, flexible

indicators.note: the exercises keep, that is hold within them, the turned word

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercises

indicators.note: a somersault turns the word for nick head over heels, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to nick a suspect is to nail or arrest them

explanation.surface: A gymnast's workouts keep someone called Nick supple as he somersaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is a verb meaning arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliant bends easily, a direct synonym of supple or flexible.

clue.text: Trio playing around noon stop the noise briefly

indicators.note: the rearranged trio goes around the other letters, holding them inside
playing suggests the letters of trio being played about with, rearranged

parts.note: sh is the call to stop the noise, a demand for quiet

explanation.surface: A musical trio is told to keep the noise down at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop the noise' is a whole command standing for the hush sound; 'playing' looks musical but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to put it in a few words, a summing-up equivalent to briefly.

clue.text: Race that lasts 31 days — a skimpy item of clothing no good

parts.note: March, abbreviated Mar, is a month of 31 days

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is taken away from the garment

parts.note: a thong is a skimpy piece of underwear or swimwear

explanation.surface: A month-long race run in minimal clothing sounds like a bad idea.
explanation.walkthrough: THONG loses G (good) because of 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long-distance running race of about 26 miles.

clue.text: Indifferent plan one avoided following

indicators.note: one being avoided means the letter for one is left out of the plan

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is short for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs at a plan that a single person skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEA without I (one) gives DEA, then F.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deaf to pleas is to be unmoved by them, so the word can mean heedless or uncaring.

clue.text: School head defends country's uprising, given sequence of events

parts.note: S can stand for school

indicators.note: the outer letters defend, surround and protect, the turned country

parts.note: a CEO, chief executive officer, is the head of a company

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the country is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Iran is the country; the 's stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A headteacher shields the school from news of a revolt abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uprising' reads the country from the bottom up; the 's of 'country's' is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline or imagined course of events, a sequence of happenings.

clue.text: Having retired, their beards contain food

indicators.note: Having retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
the two clue words contain the letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Retired men's beards are full of crumbs of food.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'contain food' as the definition, but 'contain' is the hidden-word signal and 'food' alone defines the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese, an example of food.

clue.text: Dan arranged info held by Net-based property company?

indicators.note: the inner letters are held by, contained in, the outer word

parts.note: lacy fabric is net-like, based on a net

indicators.note: arranged signals the letters of Dan being put in a new order

parts.note: gen is slang for information

explanation.surface: Dan sets up the details for an online estate agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net-based' suggests the internet; it means lace-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A land agency manages or sells estates, so it is a firm dealing in property.

clue.text: Area of US showing outrage, as addicts kidnap Greek character

parts.note: to appal is to shock or outrage

indicators.note: the addicts kidnap, take into their midst, the Greek letter

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a group of recovering addicts
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A US region is shocked as drug users abduct a Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalachia is the mountainous region of the eastern United States.

clue.text: Start to fall in French bog

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

parts.note: en is French for in

explanation.surface: Someone begins to fall into a marsh in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A fen is low marshy land, a synonym of bog.

clue.text: Chip worktop

definitions.meaning: a gambling token used in place of money
a kitchen or shop surface for working or serving

explanation.definitionFit: A gaming chip is a token, and a kitchen surface is also called by the same word.

clue.text: In what way Shakespeare initially bypassed actor in 8/11/12

parts.note: how asks in what way

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is bypassed, skipped

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: Someone asks how Shakespeare was passed over in casting.
explanation.walkthrough: 8/11/12 is BRIEF ENCOUNTER, the 1945 film.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor Howard starred as the doctor in the film Brief Encounter.

clue.text: Gusts over Delhi ruined part of Buick?

indicators.note: in a down clue the gusts go over, above, the next piece

parts.note: gusts are winds

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of Delhi are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Storms over Delhi wreck an American car.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Buick, a US car make, is an example; windshield is the American word for windscreen.
explanation.definitionFit: A windshield is the front glass of a car, so it is a component of a Buick.

clue.text: Pardon what you do after admitting burglary primarily

indicators.note: the solving piece comes after the initials
primarily takes the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: what you, the crossword solver, do is solve clues

explanation.surface: A burglar is pardoned after confessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what you do' addresses the solver, whose job is to solve.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to free from guilt or blame, a synonym of pardon.

clue.text: A way of congratulating friends?

parts.note: a hearty pat on the back congratulates, and friends are pals, spelt backwards giving a slap word

explanation.walkthrough: The cryptic reading: friends (PALS) written back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty pat on someone's back is a gesture of congratulation.

clue.text: European writer sees two rivers overlapping

indicators.note: overlapping means the two names share a letter where they meet, so one copy goes

parts.note: the Volta in Ghana and the Aire in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A writer from Europe sees two rivers meet.
explanation.walkthrough: VOLTA ends and AIRE begins with A, so they share it.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire was the pen name of the 18th-century French author and philosopher.

clue.text: Knocked over tiny teacher continually

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned upside down, so the word for tiny is read backwards

parts.note: nano is a prefix meaning very small
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A very small teacher keeps being knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked over' turns only the first piece; the teacher follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means without stopping, at tedious length, a synonym of continually.

clue.text: Voter wanting Jack to oust Liberal in a particular seat

indicators.note: the jack is brought in to oust, replace, the liberal

parts.note: an elector is a voter
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: A voter wants a man named Jack to unseat the Liberal MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' suits the election surface, but the seat is in an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejector seat throws a pilot clear of the aircraft, so the word names a kind of seat.

clue.text: Card drawer cracking at the edges in factory

indicators.note: the edge letters go in the factory word

parts.note: a mill is a factory

indicators.note: at the edges takes the first and last letters of cracking

explanation.surface: A card designer is cracking up in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald McGill drew saucy British seaside postcards.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald McGill drew comic postcards, so he was a drawer of cards.

clue.text: Actress in 8/11/12 can kid

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet
a kid is a child, here a son

explanation.surface: An actress from the film is able to joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can kid' reads as 'is able to tease'; both words are nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Celia Johnson played the heroine Laura in the film Brief Encounter.

clue.text: Mark, perhaps texting bird about unknown pub

indicators.note: the bird goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: a hen is a bird
Y is a mathematical unknown
PH is short for public house, a pub

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark is texting a girlfriend about an unfamiliar pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name; it is a punctuation mark, one used in typing and texting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphen is a short dash of punctuation, a mark that may well turn up in typed messages.

clue.text: Capital that's essential to manage Aussie beauty

indicators.note: the essential part of each word is its centre, the middle two letters

explanation.surface: Money is vital for managing an Australian beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money; it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Resort box by telephone

indicators.note: heard by telephone, the word is spoken, so it sounds the same

parts.note: to ... is to box

explanation.surface: A holiday resort is booked by a phone box.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the R of SPAR is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town with mineral springs, a kind of health resort.

clue.text: Top marks secured by expert

indicators.note: the marks are secured by, held inside, the expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert
M is short for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An expert earns the highest marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point, the peak or summit.

clue.text: Parish rector, neglecting soldiers, disturbed another cleric

indicators.note: disturbed signals the remaining letters being thrown into a new order
neglecting means the soldiers are left out of the letters

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A parish rector who ignores the troops upsets a fellow clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: PARISH RECTOR minus OR leaves PARISHRECT, which 'disturbed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An archpriest is a senior priest, a further clergyman beside the rector.

clue.text: Fictional detective faces domestic stress

indicators.note: the detective faces, stands in front of, the next piece

parts.note: Mike Hammer is Mickey Spillane's private eye
home means domestic, as in home affairs

explanation.surface: A detective in a novel faces strain at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point firmly into someone's mind is to stress or emphasise it.

clue.text: Unproductive director of 8/11/12

definitions.meaning: yielding little, as a poor year or harvest
David ... directed the film Brief Encounter

explanation.definitionFit: Lean years are meagre ones, and David Lean directed the 1945 film.
